first_description: The molecule consists of a phenyl ring attached through a two-carbon ethyl linker to an amino nitrogen, which is directly bonded to a carbon of a fused bicyclic heteroaromatic system. The bicyclic unit contains a six-membered aromatic ring with one ring nitrogen and a five-membered aromatic ring bearing an NH group, these two rings sharing one carbon–carbon bond. The ethylamino chain connects the benzene ring to the six-membered component of the fused system. The benzene ring is unsubstituted, and no stereochemistry is specified. The aromatic rings and the ethyl chain form a predominantly hydrophobic region, while the secondary amine NH provides a limited polar, hydrogen-bonding site.

first_description: The compound features a fused bicyclic aromatic scaffold formed by a benzene ring and a six-membered heteroaromatic ring containing two adjacent nitrogen atoms. A single carbon–carbon bond connects this fused system to a separate six-membered aromatic ring bearing one nitrogen, and this latter ring also carries an isopropylamino group and a methyl group on adjacent carbon atoms. The extended aromatic surfaces and the alkyl substituents create a relatively hydrophobic region, while the methoxy oxygens and the secondary amino nitrogen introduce limited polar character.

first_description: This molecule contains a central benzene ring substituted with a methylaminomethyl group, an alkynyl chain, and a phenoxy group. The methylaminomethyl substituent attaches through a CH2–NH–CH3 sequence. The alkynyl substituent consists of a four-carbon chain with a triple bond between the first two carbons followed by two methylene units, terminating at the nitrogen of a morpholine ring. The phenoxy group connects to a second benzene ring that carries a para-fluoro and an ortho-chloro substituent relative to the ether oxygen. On the central ring, the methylaminomethyl and phenoxy groups are ortho, while the alkynyl and phenoxy groups are para. The morpholine and amine groups provide polar sites, whereas the aromatic rings and alkynyl chain form a hydrophobic segment.

first_description: The structure is built around a benzene ring bearing a methoxy group, a piperazine ring, and an anilino-type NH linker to a six-membered aromatic ring containing two nitrogen atoms separated by one carbon. The piperazine is saturated and has two nitrogens: one is directly attached to the benzene ring, and the other carries an acetyl group (C(=O)CH3). The diazine-like ring is further substituted by a fused bicyclic heteroaromatic unit through a carbon–carbon bond. This fused unit comprises a five-membered aromatic ring with an NH and a six-membered aromatic ring containing one nitrogen, sharing one bond. The acetylated piperazine and NH groups contribute polar character amid the extensive aromatic hydrophobic framework.

first_description: The molecule contains a benzene ring substituted with a methyl group, a nitro group, and a sulfonyl group. The methyl and nitro groups are para to each other, while the sulfonyl group is ortho to the methyl and meta to the nitro. The nitro group is encoded with a positively charged nitrogen and a negatively charged oxygen. The sulfonyl sulfur is bonded to a nitrogen that carries a 2-(piperidin-1-yl)ethyl chain and an E-configured N=CH linkage. This linkage connects through the CH carbon to a fused bicyclic heteroaromatic system composed of a five-membered ring with two adjacent nitrogens and a six-membered ring with one nitrogen, sharing one bond. A cyano group is attached to the six-membered ring of this fused unit. The nitro, sulfonyl, piperidine, and cyano groups contribute polar character, while the aromatic rings and ethylene chain provide hydrophobic regions.

first_description: Two benzene rings are linked through an E-vinylsulfonamide chain. The first benzene ring carries two acetoxy substituents positioned ortho to one another, and a vinylsulfonyl substituent located para to one acetoxy group and meta to the other. The carbon–carbon double bond of the vinyl unit has specified E geometry. The sulfonyl sulfur is bonded to the vinyl carbon and to an NH group, which in turn connects to an ethylene chain ending at the second, unsubstituted benzene ring. The two acetoxy groups and the sulfonamide NH/SO2 unit create polar hydrogen-bonding sites, while the two phenyl rings provide hydrophobic aromatic regions separated by this polar linker.

first_description: A para-methoxyphenyl group is attached directly to a five-membered aromatic ring containing one nitrogen atom. first_description: A saturated polycyclic nitrogen-containing cage is formed by several fused and bridged six- and five-membered rings that share a common tertiary amine nitrogen. One cage carbon carries a methyl ester, and another carbon is connected through an exocyclic double bond with specified Z geometry to a six-membered aromatic diazine ring. This diazine ring contains two nitrogen atoms and bears two methoxy substituents; its remaining aromatic carbon is the point of attachment to the alkene. first_description: This molecule contains two benzene rings connected directly through a single bond, forming a biphenyl-type scaffold. One benzene ring carries a nitrile substituent and, para to it, a methylene group linked to a 1,2,4-triazole ring through one of its nitrogen atoms. The same benzene ring is further substituted ortho to the nitrile by the second benzene ring. The second benzene ring bears a sulfamate group, in which an oxygen attached to the ring is connected to a sulfur atom carrying an amino group and two doubly bonded oxygens, and a chlorine atom ortho to the sulfamate. The molecule therefore combines a nitrile, a nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic ring, and a polar sulfamate on a halogenated biphenyl scaffold. The nitrogen-containing heteroarene and sulfamate contribute a relatively polar region, while the aromatic rings provide a hydrophobic framework.

One carbon adjacent to the sulfur carries a methylene-linked 3,5-difluorophenyl group; the other carbon adjacent to sulfur bears a secondary aminomethyl substituent, and the remaining carbon attached to the nitrogen carries a phenyl group. The aminomethyl chain connects through its nitrogen to the benzene ring of a 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran, where the benzene is fused to a five-membered nonaromatic ring containing oxygen and two methylene units. first_description: This molecule consists of a saturated five-membered oxygen heterocycle (a tetrahydrofuran ring) attached through one of its carbon atoms to a nitrogen of a purine system. The purine is amino-substituted at the six-membered ring; its five-membered imidazole ring provides the N-linkage. On the tetrahydrofuran ring, one carbon bears a methoxy group, another bears a phosphate monoester (-O-P(=O)(OH)2), and a third carries a phosphooxymethyl substituent (-CH2-O-P(=O)(OH)2). All four carbon stereocenters in the tetrahydrofuran ring have been assigned R configuration. The two phosphate groups and the amino-substituted purine create a strongly polar, hydrogen-bonding region with multiple acidic hydroxyl and heteroaromatic nitrogen centers, whereas the methoxy group and saturated ring contribute little hydrophobic character. No formal charges are encoded.

This saturated five-membered thiazolidine also contains a sulfur atom, and its carbon adjacent to sulfur carries an amide chain: -C(=O)-NH-CH2- attached to a fluorinated chlorinated phenyl ring. That chiral carbon is assigned S configuration. The pendant benzene ring has a fluorine ortho to the methylene attachment and a chlorine meta to the methylene attachment, with the chlorine and fluorine ortho to each other. The indole system is further substituted on its fused benzene ring with a fluorine. Multiple urea, amide, and carbamoyl groups, along with heteroaromatic nitrogens, form a polar hydrogen-bonding region; the fluorinated aryl and indole rings provide an aromatic, relatively lipophilic segment. No formal charges are present.

first_description: The molecule contains a five-membered saturated ring with two nitrogen atoms and two carbonyl carbons, forming a diaza-dione core. One nitrogen carries an ethyl group, and the other nitrogen is substituted with a benzyl group. The para position of that benzyl phenyl ring is directly connected to a pyridine ring; this pyridine is disubstituted such that both substituents occupy positions adjacent to the ring nitrogen. One pyridine substituent is the aforementioned phenyl ring, and the other is a cyclohexylmethyl group attached through a methylene bridge. Thus, the overall structure includes the polar carbonyl-containing heterocycle linked through an aromatic spacer to a pyridine bearing a cyclohexylmethyl substituent. The cyclohexylmethyl and phenyl/pyridine segments form a relatively hydrophobic region, while the two carbonyls and two nitrogens of the saturated ring provide a polar hydrogen-bonding segment. No stereocenters or formal charges are specified.

No formal charges are encoded.

The heteroaromatic ring carries a secondary amine substituent that extends to a chiral carbon specified as having S configuration. That carbon is attached to an N,N-dimethylaminomethyl group and to a phenyl ring substituted with fluorine at the meta position relative to the point of attachment. first_description: An N-ethylpiperazine ring is attached through one of its nitrogen atoms to a benzene ring that also carries a chlorine and an amide-linked pentafluorophenyl group. The piperazine nitrogen is para to the amide-bearing carbon and ortho to the chlorine on that benzene ring. The amide linkage consists of an NH group on the benzene connected to the carbonyl carbon of a fully fluorinated benzene ring, so the second aromatic ring bears five fluorine substituents on its remaining carbon atoms. The central benzene ring thus displays a substitution pattern in which the piperazine and amide are opposite one another, with chlorine adjacent to the piperazine. The N-ethyl substituent and the pentafluorophenyl ring create a hydrophobic, electron-poor region, while the piperazine tertiary amines and the amide provide polar functionality. No stereocenters are specified.

first_description: The molecule is built around a seven-membered partially unsaturated ring containing two nitrogens and fused to a benzene ring. This bicyclic core carries an N-methyl carboxamide, an imine carbon substituted with a phenyl group, and a chiral carbon with R configuration that bears a urea substituent. The urea nitrogen links to a benzene ring, and on that benzene ring a meta position carries a long polar linker: a benzyl carbamate connected to a glycinamide unit, followed by a propyl ether. The ether oxygen is attached to another benzene ring, which also carries a piperidinylmethyl substituent meta to the ether attachment. The linker thus includes carbamate, amide, and ether groups, creating a flexible, hydrogen-bonding segment between the two aromatic rings, while the fused bicyclic and phenyl groups form a large hydrophobic region.

first_description: The molecule is built around two benzene rings connected through a trisubstituted alkene. A central sp2 carbon is attached to both aryl rings and doubly bonded to a methine that bears an isopropyl group, with E stereochemistry specified across that double bond. On one benzene ring, para to the alkene attachment, there is a 2-(diethylamino)ethoxy substituent, where the oxygen is linked to an ethyl chain ending in a tertiary diethylamino group. The other benzene ring carries a hydroxy group para to the alkene attachment. The hydroxy group can act as a hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor, and the amino nitrogen can accept hydrogen bonds.

On one benzene ring, para to the alkene attachment, there is a 2-(diethylamino)ethoxy substituent, where the oxygen is linked to an ethyl chain ending in a tertiary diethylamino group. The other benzene ring carries a hydroxy group para to the alkene attachment. This arrangement creates a relatively hydrophobic region from the two aromatic rings and the isopropyl-substituted alkene, while the tertiary amino ether and phenolic hydroxy provide a more polar segment. The hydroxy group can act as a hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor, and the amino nitrogen can accept hydrogen bonds.

first_description: The structure contains five separate rings linked by single bonds and an amide linker. A 1,2,3-triazole ring bears a (1S)-1-(trifluoromethyl)ethyl group on one nitrogen, and is directly connected through one of its carbons to a thiazole ring. The thiazole is linked via an amide: the thiazole carbon is attached to the amide nitrogen, and the carbonyl carbon is attached to a pyridine ring. That pyridine ring also carries a dimethylamino group and an imidazole ring on separate carbons. The imidazole ring has a cyclopropyl substituent on a carbon. The cluster of nitrogen-containing heteroaromatic rings with the amide, dimethylamino, and trifluoromethyl groups creates a strongly polar region, while the cyclopropane and methyl portions contribute a small hydrophobic segment. The stereocenter at the trifluoromethyl-bearing carbon is specified as S.

first_description: The compound features a six-membered aromatic ring containing two nitrogen atoms, one as an NH group; it bears an exocyclic carbonyl, an azetidine ring attached through its nitrogen, a secondary amino group connecting to a cyclopentane, and a thiazole ring fused to a benzene ring via a single bond. The cyclopentane ring is heavily substituted: at one carbon it is linked through NH to the central diazine-like ring, at another it has a hydroxymethyl group, and at two additional carbons it has secondary hydroxy groups. first_description: The molecule contains three aromatic rings connected by a central urea group and a diaryl ether.
